label: Resilience
blurb: Condition and exposure: how modified the basin's wetlands are, projected intactness in 2050, and projected warming and dry-season drying.

headlines.label: Resilience score (provisional)
headlines.note: Mean of this pillar's variable percentiles among basins at this level, 0–100

charts.title: Percentile by variable
charts.subtitle: Percentiles run from 0 to 100 among all basins at this level, and higher is better for the pillar.

charts.title: Distribution across basins

charts.label: label

method: Human modification is the mean of gHM (~2016, 0–1) over the basin's wetland, weighting each res-8 cell by its wetland area; more modification ranks lower, and a basin with no mapped wetland has no value. Projected intactness is GLOBIO 4 mean species abundance for 2050 under SSP5-RCP8.5, area-weighted over the basin; more intact ranks higher. Climate exposure compares CHELSA 2.1 for 2041–2070 under SSP3-7.0 (median of five models) with 1981–2010: warming is the change in annual mean temperature (more warming ranks lower), and dry-season rainfall is the relative change in precipitation of the driest quarter (drier ranks lower), both area-weighted over the basin. Basins with no dry-season rainfall in the baseline have no value for the second. Basins are HydroBASINS v1c polygons as H3 res-6 cells (~36 km²): level-6 basins are filled by cell centre and coarser levels are unions of level-6 basins by Pfafstetter code. Wetland is GLWD v2 classes 8–32 (lacustrine, riverine, palustrine, ephemeral, peatland and coastal wetlands); open water and rice paddies are left out. Scores are mid-rank percentiles (0–100) among the basins at the chosen level, with direction applied so higher is better for the pillar; tied values share the midpoint of their rank range. The pillar score is the plain mean of the variable percentiles. All of this is provisional: which variables belong to which pillar, and how they are weighted, has not been decided.
